observations: Photo shows a bare automotive engine assembly (block, turbo, wiring harness, injector pump) sitting on a dark floor.
No manufacturer plate, engine code, or VIN sticker is legible anywhere in the frame.
Image has a visible watermark 'CAMON 40' and camera EXIF text overlay, not seller-applied documentation.
No compression gauge, running video, or odometer/mileage sticker visible.
No accessories (alternator pulley belt, starter motor) clearly shown as included or excluded.

claims.evidence: No import paperwork, auction sheet, or shipping tag visible in photo 0.
No warranty card, shop stamp, or written terms shown in photo 0.

risks.risk: Engine model/displacement unknown, which drives most of the price difference between engine types.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the engine code/plate or casting number stamped on the block.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this, since even a worst-case range depends on knowing the model

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal damage (compression, timing, crank issues) not visible externally.
risks.proof: Video of the engine actually starting and running, or a compression test printout.

risks.risk: Mileage/usage history on the engine is unknown.
risks.proof: Photo of the odometer or Japan auction sheet with recorded km.

risks.risk: 'Direct Japan' origin claim cannot be confirmed, affecting trust in low-mileage/low-wear assumptions.
risks.proof: Photo of the import auction sheet, bill of lading, or customs paperwork.
risks.if_unproven: treated as unverified local-market unit, not premium Japan-import

risks.risk: Completeness of the engine (turbo, injectors, sensors, loom) not confirmed as all original/working.
risks.proof: Full 360° photos with all attached parts labeled, plus a parts list from seller.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/casting number or manufacturer plate.
Video of the engine running (cold start preferred).
Photo of Japan auction sheet or import documentation showing mileage and grade.
Written warranty terms or shop receipt showing the 2-month guarantee.
Additional angle photos showing turbo, injectors, and wiring harness fully.
response.reason: The engine's model/type cannot be read from the photo, and model is the primary driver of price for engines, so even a worst-case figure is not possible until the engine code or plate is shown.
